system.summary: An 8 x 8 turning grille (Fleissner) with 16 holes: blocks of 64 cipher letters written row by row and read through the holes, quarter turns clockwise, last block filled with nulls (x y z); the key was proposed by an AI model from the ciphertext and is not validated.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on the sheets or in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1 (its p. 11 notes space for six telegrams still to be translated). No card of the fonds reads these telegrams.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish. Claude (Opus) agents transcribed the telegrams from the CEHM viewer images and ran the preregistered measure; after the project's own attempts (columnar transposition, Caesar shifts, the cards of the fonds) failed, an AI model (Claude Fable 5.2, one API run, named in the contributor's files) proposed the grille and the readings from three telegrams, with one telegram held out; the agents checked the grille with an independent decoder and ran the measure once (failed). No human palaeographer checked the transcriptions. Issue #502 (SeldomPhooey, AI agents) added the held-out telegram's reading, the outside check and two transcription corrections; an independent session checked them against the images on 13 Nov 2026.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, Clave G.A. validation and readings, grille check and measure, write-up)
Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), one API run on 1551.3-4, 1561.5-13 and 1569.3-10 (grille proposal and readings; pointed out the joined groups of 1561.7-13)

solution.what: Telegrams 1551.3-4, 1561.5-13, 1569.3-10 and the held-out 1561.3-13 transcribed from the CEHM viewer images and hashed before any key was tried (1561.7-13, which turned out to be in the Clave G.A., was transcribed in the same pass).
Every card of the fonds tried on 1551.3-4, 1561.5-13, 1569.3-10, 1561.7-13 and 1561.2-13, decoding group by group: none reads them (best coverage 0.50 < 0.70).
Simple columnar transposition, widths 2-15, on 1569.3-10; Caesar shifts on 1561.5-13: no Spanish.

Claude Fable 5.2 (one API run, 1561.3-13 held out): 8 x 8 turning grille, holes derived from the nulls X/Z of the second block of 1551.3-4; one grille for 1551.3-4, 1561.5-13 and 1569.3-10; and 1561.7-13 is the Clave G.A. once the coded groups are joined.

Grille checked with our own decoder: five blocks of 64 letters (1551.3-4 both, 1561.5-13 first, 1569.3-10 first two) give Spanish with no insertion or deletion, with six letters corrected by the sense (listo, atacar, nuestro, por, contrario, and a doubled v in convendria); two declared repairs (one deletion in 1561.5-13, one insertion in 1569.3-10) for the shifted blocks.

Preregistered single measure of the grille on the held-out telegram 1561.3-13 (127 letters): car4 0.520 vs threshold 0.70; best of 400 controls 0.402 (200 random grilles), margin +0.118 vs +0.30 required: NOT validated. Cause: a letter lost in the group YPXB shifts the second block; the first block reads. A post-hoc trial is not counted.

Words counted by the README rule, strictly (restored, probable-by-sense and unresolved words are not read): 1551.3-4 16 of 17, 1561.5-13 9 of 17, 1569.3-10 23 of 26: 48 of 60 = 80%. The contributor's count (97% before, 95% in the file) takes the 9 probable words as read.

Integration check by an independent session: own Fleissner decoder from key.txt reproduces every block of decryption.txt; 0 of 2000 random grilles of the same family (one hole per rotation orbit) score as well as this grille on the five fluent blocks (Spanish 4-gram, per letter: this grille -4.65, best random -7.10, mean -8.06); the grille was fitted on these blocks, so this shows fit and not validation. The held-out telegram 1561.3-13 is not in the repository, so the failed measure could not be re-run.
Housekeeping: Split out of mccarty1911 (one key, one entry): the Clave G.A. digraphic card and the turning grille are different systems; mccarty1911 keeps the two telegrams in the card.

Issue #502 (SeldomPhooey, AI agents, two independent transcriptions): the cipher of the held-out telegram 1561.3-13 published for the first time (26 groups, 127 letters), and two corrections of the first transcription, IRRXNO in 1569.3-10 and ERDEO in 1551.3-4.

Independent check of issue #502: own decoder written from the grid reproduces the table of block 2 of 1561.3-13 at the placeholder positions 94-98 and the 192-letter decryption of 1569.3-10; images fetched from the CEHM viewer: 1561.3-13 matches the issue group by group, 1569.3-10 reads irrxno (two r's), 1551.3-4 reads erdeo; BNM typed copy fetched (SHA-256 f37754c2...).

1561.3-13 read in both blocks with one placeholder letter inserted at index 96 of the cipher (inside YPXB); the position is chosen by reading among positions 94-98 (95 breaks hay, 97 breaks probabilidades), tardanza and probabilidades each need a letter corrected, parras is unresolved: 14 of 17 words sure. The repair does not turn the failed measure into a pass.

Outside check of the grille: the typed period copy of 1569.3-10 (BNM AMA Ms.M/T.2260 c.21) against the grille's decryption of the 192 letters: 174 of 176 letters identical (t for p, a doubled v, an i in lograriase); the copy was not used to find the grille. Confirms all 64 cells of the grille, not the word cuts of the other telegrams.

Own control, not the preregistered statistic: block 1 of 1561.3-13 (64 letters, never sent to the model) under the grille scores -4.36 per letter (Spanish 4-gram, es-modern) against -6.54 for the best of 300 random grilles of the same family (mean -7.79). For block 2 the language-model score alone does not pick index 96; the position rests on words.

Words recounted by the README rule, strictly: 1551.3-4 17 of 17, 1561.5-13 9 of 17, 1569.3-10 24 of 26, 1561.3-13 14 of 17: 64 of 77 = 83%. The first contributor's looser count (probable words as read) gives 74 of 77.

validation.notes: The preregistered single measure on the held-out telegram CMXV.16.1561.3-13 FAILED: car4 = 0.520 against the 0.70 threshold, margin +0.118 over the best of 400 controls against the +0.30 required (200 random grilles at most 0.402, 200 shuffled texts at most 0.299); the lost letter in YPXB shifts block 2; the post-hoc trial is not counted. Contributor's own test, not docs/_validate.py; the cipher is now published (issue #502) but the measure was not re-run. Separately, an outside check succeeded: a typed period copy of 1569.3-10 (BNM, AMA Ms.M/T.2260 c.21) agrees with the grille's decryption on 174 of 176 letters; it was not used to find the grille.

outcome.method_basis: The grille was proposed by an AI model in one API run from the ciphertext of three telegrams (the holes follow the nulls x/z of 1551.3-4) and checked here with an independent decoder; the held-out telegram was not sent. The preregistered measure on that telegram failed. An outside document, a typed period copy of 1569.3-10 (BNM), later agreed with the decryption on 174 of 176 letters and was not used to find the grille. The grille rests also on six 64-letter blocks that read as Spanish with no insertion or deletion, and on the first block of the held-out telegram.

outcome.notes: Four telegrams of 18-20 April 1911 read in part with a turning grille that an AI model proposed; the preregistered measure on a held-out telegram FAILED (0.520 against 0.70; margin +0.118 against +0.30) and stays reported as failed. The grille was later checked by an outside document, a typed period copy of 1569.3-10 (174 of 176 letters). By the README rule (words, strict) 64 of 77 = 83%; the first contributor's looser count takes probable words as read (74 of 77). Order of events (hashes in the files, single commits) is by the contributor's record. The same traffic's Clave G.A. telegrams are on mccarty1911 (a different cipher).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration count by words (README rule), from reading.md, 13 Nov 2026: 77 words, 64 sure = 83% (1551.3-4 17 of 17, 1561.5-13 9 of 17, 1569.3-10 24 of 26, 1561.3-13 14 of 17; 10 probable, 3 unresolved are not counted as read). The first contributor's looser figure counts the probable words as read: 74 of 77 = 96%; SeldomPhooey's own figure for 1561.3-13 is 14 of 17 strict, 16 of 17 with the probable words.

texts.label: Four telegrams of 18-20 April 1911 in the turning grille (CEHM-Carso CMXV.16.1551.3-4, 1561.3-13, 1561.5-13, 1569.3-10)
texts.summary: San Antonio and El Paso, 18-20 April 1911, before Ciudad Juárez: water for the forces and funds; an armistice would destroy the insurgent forces and Juárez should be attacked if success is likely; Dr ready to attack Juárez, armistice probable, funds insufficient; an American officer advises against assaulting a mined Juárez and for attacking in three eight-hour shifts. The grille is checked by a typed copy of one telegram.

reading_review.note: Read as Spanish sentences: 1561.5-13 has five letters corrected by the sense and two single S unresolved; 1561.3-13 needs a placeholder letter and two letters corrected, parras unresolved; the one declared repair left in 1569.3-10 is gone with IRRXNO. Strict count by words 64 of 77 = 83%.
